correctness.rationale: The exact gcd theorem of Komatsu–Song identifies d_j=a/gcd(a,M_j), M_j=(1/2)lcm{m:phi(m)<=2j}. Every distinct p>=5 dividing a has first occurrence in M_j at j=(p-1)/2 (since any multiple has totient at least p-1); thresholds are distinct and <=J_n; each forces a distinct strict drop. Since the product of strict gcd ratios is a and each nontrivial drop contributes a factor >=2, 1+omega_(>=5)(a)<=T<=1+Omega(a), giving the specified absolute bound relative to omega(n(n-1)). For odd p, p^k|a with k>=2 means n=0 or 1 mod p^k, and for 2 the modulus shifts; summing the geometric prime power probabilities plus O(sqrt(X)log X/X) residue errors gives mean Omega(a)-omega(a)=O(1). For Y=X^((loglog X)^(-1/3)), CRT simultaneously models any fixed number of prime-divisibility indicators as independent Bernoulli(2/p) up to X^{-1+o(1)} fixed moments, with mean and variance 2loglog X+O(logloglog X). Primes>Y dividing n(n-1)<=X^2 contribute <=2(loglog X)^(1/3)=o(sqrt(loglog X); Slutsky and Markov give the Gaussian. Independent exact Stirling/gcd computations n=4..90 verified 87 cases but do not prove the CLT.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS for the new active-filtration-count gaussian law and deterministic number-theoretic sandwich in the natural unsigned Stirling semigroup. Komatsu–Song (October 2, 2026) exactly prove the gcd filtration and telescopic Apéry representation; that is essential prior work. Classical Erdős–Kac and CRT prove additive prime-factor CLTs, but applying them to T requires the nontrivial p>=5 first-appearance threshold, repeated-prime bounds, and mismatch control. A very short unstated corollary or later extension of Komatsu–Song could subsume this; retained priority risk. Importantly, T is NOT the minimal embedding dimension in general.

It is neither just plugging a generic random integer into Erdős–Kac nor claiming minimal generators incorrectly.
